answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post copper-backed collateral and earn reputation through long-lived, cross-agent attestations. At random, a zenith node issues costly challenge tasks whose answers are checked against independent peers; cloned identities cannot cheaply manufacture diverse, consistent histories. A fake swarm must therefore lock substantial capital in every account, pay operating costs over time, and risk automatic slashing when one coordinated error exposes the vine of identities.
